name: random loss
why: The reference run: a minute of 3% independent loss and 10 ms of average jitter over a 40 ms buffer. FEC rebuilds most frames that miss their slot, so 0.7% are concealed and no gap is longer than one frame. Seeded, so this pins the model rather than a hand calculation; the properties in index.test.ts hold across seeds.

name: bursts of three
why: The same loss rate in bursts averaging three packets. FEC reaches back one packet, so inside a burst only the last frame can be rebuilt: concealment doubles against random loss and the longest gap grows from 20 ms to 160 ms.

name: bursts, deeper buffer
why: An 80 ms buffer gives the second RED copy, which leaves 40 ms after its frame, time to arrive. With RED reaching back two packets, concealment falls below the random-loss run with FEC, at the price of 40 ms more delay on every frame.

why: 30 ms of average jitter over a 40 ms buffer: over a quarter of packets arrive after their slot, and the buffer, not the loss, is the problem. FEC rebuilds about half of them; the rest are concealed.

name: loss of 100% leaves nothing to simulate
why: Every packet lost is not a network a jitter buffer can do anything about, and the Gilbert model divides by 1 - loss.

expect.message: Loss must be at least 0% and below 100%.

name: a burst shorter than one packet is not a burst
why: Burst length is the average number of packets a loss takes; below 1 it has no meaning.

expect.message: Bursts average at least one packet: 1 means losses are independent.

name: an unknown protection scheme is named
why: The select only offers four; a host writing another value gets told which ones exist.

expect.message: Protection must be one of none, fec, red1, red2.
